docs.title: Spline IK
docs.text:
Info

This is AI-generated documentation that has not yet been human reviewed.

Builds a spline IK setup with controls placed along a curve, plus optional twist controllers. Used by the Skirt - Spline, Hair - Spline, and Tail - Spline assemblies.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Creates a hidden curve that runs along the chain, and a set of controls evenly spaced along it. Moving a control bends the curve, and the chain follows the curve. The controls can only be moved; rotation and scale are locked.

Twist controllers can be added at the start, end, or every control. Twist controllers only rotate around their length. Twist is blended along the chain between neighboring twist controllers.

Like the standard IK, spline IK drives the MCH-IK bones created by the FK/IK switch, so the chain can be switched between FK and spline IK.

Note

Spline IK does not support FK <> IK snapping. A spline IK pose often cannot match an FK chain. Limb twist bones are also unavailable; use the spline twist controllers instead.

Image placeholder

image/spline_ik.png — A Hair - Spline assembly in Pose mode with IK enabled, showing the sphere controls along the chain and the twist widgets on each control. Ideally the middle control is moved so the chain is visibly bent.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• Spline Control Count: the number of controls along the curve. Controls are always placed at the start and end of the chain, with the rest evenly spaced between them. Default: 3 (4 for Tail - Spline). Range: 2-10.
  • Twist Type: where to create twist controllers. Default: Start and End (All for Hair - Spline).
    • None: no twist controllers.
    • Start and End: twist controllers on the first and last controls.
    • Start: twist controller on the first control only.
    • End: twist controller on the last control only.
    • All: twist controllers on every control.
  • Skip First: leave the first bone out of the spline. The first bone stays attached to the parent of the chain and the spline starts at the second bone. Useful for skirts, where the top of the skirt should stay attached to the hips. Default: off (on for Skirt - Spline).
  • Skip Last: leave the last bone out of the spline. The last bone gets an FK control instead. Default: off.
  • Tip Widget: the custom bone shape for the last bone when Skip Last is enabled. Default: CIRCLE. See widgets.

docs.title: Standard IK
docs.text:
Info

This is AI-generated documentation that has not yet been human reviewed.

Builds a standard IK chain with an IK control and a pole target. Used by the Arm and Leg assemblies.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Creates the IK chain that drives the MCH-IK bones created by the FK/IK switch. The last bone of the IK chain becomes the IK control (the hand or foot), and the bones before it are solved by the IK. With the default IK bone count of 3, that's two IK bones (upper arm and forearm) and the hand as the control.

A pole target is created automatically and placed out from the middle joint (the elbow or knee) in the direction the chain bends. A line is drawn from the pole to the joint so it's easy to see which joint it belongs to.

Tip

Model the limb with a slight bend at the elbow or knee. The bend tells the tool which direction the joint should bend and where to place the pole. A perfectly straight limb will still work, but the pole may end up on the wrong side.

Any bones in the chain past the IK control (like the toe on a leg) get their own FK control that is shared between FK and IK.

The IK chain can stretch past its rest length. This can be turned off by the animator with the IK Stretch property in the Rig Properties panel. Stretch is on by default.

FK <> IK snapping is set up automatically.

Image placeholder

image/standard_ik.png — An arm assembly in Pose mode with IK enabled, showing the IK control on the hand, the pole target behind the elbow, and the line connecting the pole to the elbow.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• IK Bone Count: the number of bones from the start of the chain used for the IK, including the IK control. Any remaining bones get FK controls that are shared between FK and IK. Default: 3. Minimum: 2.
  • Add Foot Roll: adds a foot roll control to the IK control. Requires a heel pivot and at least one bone past the IK chain (the toe). Default: on for the Leg assembly.
  • Tip Widget: the custom bone shape for the FK controls past the IK control (the toe). Default: CIRCLE. See widgets.

docs.title: Torso FK
docs.text: Builds the torso control stack: torso/hips/chest masters, spine/neck FK, and head control from a single linear ORG chain.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The default torso configuration includes two bones for the lower torso, usually "ORG-hips" and "ORG-spine.01" or similar. These bones will be controlled by the hips controller. This default configuration also includes two bones for the upper torso, usually "ORG-spine.02" and "ORG-chest" or similar. The ORG-chest bone has 2 twist bones enabled by default (see below). These bones will be controlled by the chest controller. Lastly, the default configuration includes a single neck bone with 2 twist bones ("ORG-neck", usually), and a single head bone ("ORG-head", usually). This is a total of 6 main bones: ORG-hips, ORG-spine.01, ORG-spine.02, ORG-chest, ORG-neck, and ORG-head, and 4 twist bones: 2 for the chest and 2 for the neck.

Image placeholder

image/torso_sections.png — Labeled side view of the default torso chain, with each section bracketed: hips controller (hips, spine.01), chest controller (spine.02, chest + 2 twist bones), neck (+ 2 twist bones), and head.

This configuration can be modified to fit different torso types. It uses two parameters to determine which bones belong to which section of the torso: "Lower torso bone count" and "Neck bone count". It will always assume a head bone count of 1. So any remaining bones will belong to the chest. This should allow a decent amount of flexibility if you want to reconfigure the torso. All lower torso bones will be controlled by the hips controller, and all upper torso bones will be controlled by the chest controller. Adding additional neck bones will add additional FK controllers for the neck. This is usually not desired unless there is a really long neck. Use twist bones instead if you only want one neck FK controller.

The torso uses twist bones in a manner similar to the IK assemblies, but slightly different. The chest twist bones aren't technically twist bones. They are used primarily as a way to add an additional tweak bone without adding another FK controller. The chest twist bones do not twist; in that way they are somewhat like the shin. But there is no way to add twist capabilities to the chest, unlike the shin. The neck twist bones do twist, following the head with fall-off. This is an optional setting that can be disabled, but is usually desirable. If neck falloff is disabled, the neck twist bones will behave like the chest: adding an additional tweak bone without adding an FK controller. Twist bones are technically not required to have neck rotation fall-off from the head. All that is required is more than 1 neck bone. As stated above, though, this adds an additional FK controller for the neck, and is usually not desirable. If there is only one neck bone and no twist bones, neck fall-off cannot operate.

Image placeholder

image/torso_controls.png — The finished torso in Pose mode, showing the torso box, the hips and chest widgets, the spine FK circles, and the neck and head controls.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• Lower Torso Bone Count: the number of bones at the start of the chain that belong to the lower torso, controlled by the hips controller. Default: 2.
  • Neck Bone Count: the number of neck bones between the chest and the head. Each neck bone gets its own FK controller. Default: 1.
  • Use Twist Bones: use twist bones on the neck and chest. See twist bones. Default: on.
    • Neck Twist Bone Count: the number of twist bones on each neck bone. Default: 2.
    • Chest Twist Bone Count: the number of twist bones on the chest. Default: 2.
  • Add Neck Rotation Isolation: add rotation isolation to the neck. Default: on.
    • Neck Inherit Scale From Root: the neck takes its scale from the root bone instead of the chest. Default: on.
  • Add Head Rotation Isolation: add rotation isolation to the head. Default: on.
    • Head Inherit Scale From Root: the head takes its scale from the root bone instead of the neck. Default: on.
  • Neck Falloff: how the head's rotation fades down the neck. Set to None to disable neck fall-off. See falloff. Default: Root.

docs.title: Twist Bones (tool)
docs.text:
Info

This is AI-generated documentation that has not yet been human reviewed.

Drives twist bones along a limb segment and adds tweak controls to them. Used by the Arm and Leg assemblies.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
For each twist segment (for example, the upper arm and the forearm), the tool finds the twist bones that belong to that bone. If there aren't any, it creates them. The twist bones are then set up to pick up rotation from a control bone, with more rotation toward one end of the segment than the other. How quickly the rotation fades along the segment is set by the falloff.

Each twist bone also gets a tweak control, the same as an FK Tweak Chain. This gives arms and legs extra tweak controls along their length, even on segments that don't twist.

For concepts, creating twist bones ahead of time, and what happens when an assembly is deleted, see the main Twist Bones page.

Warning

If twist bones already exist for a segment, the twist bone count must match. Otherwise, the assembly will fail with an error.

Image placeholder

image/twist_segments.png — The Twist Segments section of the Arm redo panel, showing the twist status message, Twist Bone Count, and the segment list (Name, Index, Source, Falloff).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• Use Twist Bones: enable twist bones for the assembly. Default: on for Arm and Leg.
  • Twist Bone Count: the number of twist bones per segment. Default: 4. Range: 2-16.
  • Twist Segments: the list of limb bones that get twist bones. Each segment has:
    • Name: a label for the segment. Only used in the UI.
    • Index: which bone in the selected chain the segment belongs to, starting from 0. For an arm, 0 is the upper arm and 1 is the forearm.
    • Source: where the twist comes from.
      • Self: twist comes from the segment's own control, like the upper arm or thigh. The twist is strongest at the end of the segment, and fades out toward the shoulder or hip.
      • Child: twist comes from the next bone in the chain, like the forearm twisting with the hand.
      • None: no twist. The twist bones are only used for deformation and extra tweak controls, like the shin.
    • Falloff: how the twist fades along the segment. Not used when the source is None.

The twist status above the segment list shows whether twist bones already exist ("All twist bones present"), will be created ("Twist bones will be created"), or have a problem that needs to be fixed first.

docs.title: Falloff
docs.text:
Falloff controls how much of the twist each twist bone receives. The bone at the end of the segment always gets the full twist. The table below shows the amount of twist each bone receives with 4 twist bones, from the start of the segment to the end.

Falloff Bone 1 Bone 2 Bone 3 Bone 4 Linear 25% 50% 75% 100% Smooth 16% 50% 84% 100% Round 66% 87% 97% 100% Root 13% 29% 50% 100% Sharp 6% 25% 56% 100%

Root and Sharp keep most of the twist near the end of the segment. Round spreads the twist almost evenly along the whole segment.

Default segments:

Assembly Segment Source Falloff Arm Arm Self Root Arm Forearm Child Linear Leg Thigh Self Sharp Leg Shin None —

Widgets are the custom bone shapes used to display controls in Pose mode. Many assemblies have one or more widget parameters for choosing the shape of their controls.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
When an assembly is created, RigTools creates a widget object for each control and assigns it as the bone's custom shape. Widgets are created in a separate, hidden collection in the scene (WGT by default; see addon preferences).

Widgets belong to the assembly that created them. They are deleted when the assembly is deleted or reconfigured.

Image placeholder

image/widgets.png — A row of bones in Pose mode, each showing one of the selectable widget shapes (Circle, Rectangle, FK Shape, Box, Pill, Shoulder, IK Shape), labeled.

docs.title: Widget types
docs.text:
These are the shapes available in widget parameters (FK Widget, FK End Widget, Tip Widget, Master Controller Widget, etc.):

Widget Description Used by default for Circle A ring around the bone. Most FK controls, toes, tails Rectangle A flat, narrow rectangle along the bone. Skirt FK controls and masters FK Shape The FK limb shape. Arm and leg FK controls Box A box around the bone. — Pill A rounded, pill-shaped outline. Palm controls Shoulder A curved shoulder shape. Shoulder IK Shape The IK control shape. — None No widget. The bone is drawn normally. —

Some controls always use a fixed widget, such as the IK controls, poles, tweaks, spline controls, twist controllers, foot roll, finger curl, and the torso master controls.
